BERT4Rec’s original implementation uses full-vocabulary log-softmax, tied input/output embeddings, and cross-entropy averaged over valid masked targets. Padded target slots receive zero weight; padding is also masked in attention. Its output head nevertheless includes special-token rows. For an item-only objective, slice logits to real items and remap labels, or suppress PAD/MASK logits before softmax; ignoring padded targets alone does not remove these classes from the denominator. This is an explicit objective choice: preserve the corrected baseline’s convention during a cutoff-only comparison. [Original implementation](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/run.py)

Sampled softmax is an approximation, not interchangeable with full-softmax CE or uncorrected CE over sampled candidates. TensorFlow’s implementation uses sampling expected counts and removes accidental hits where sampled negatives equal that row’s target. Sample only real item IDs; remove target collisions per prediction, including repeated occurrences of that ID. Historical items other than the current target remain competing classes under ordinary full-softmax CE; excluding all historical items changes the objective. Preserve repeated history positions and their reconstruction targets; repeated IDs elsewhere in context are not shifted-target leakage. [Sampled-softmax documentation](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/nn/sampled_softmax_loss)

For a deliberately separate reconstruction/terminal objective, a recommended formulation is L = λr·sum(CEr)/Nr + λt·sum(CEt)/Nt, with explicit fixed weights and empty-group handling. Separate normalization prevents mask count from silently changing task balance, but differs from pooling all targets into one mean. Keep the baseline’s reduction fixed for the cutoff comparison. Hide each terminal target behind MASK and read its actual position; with left padding, never use count−1. The original implementation uses one pooled masked-target mean. [Loss reduction](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/run.py)
